> Hi Eric,

> Over the past few weeks, Aspen has gotten some new people on staff who have started entering data in the CMS. As is typically the case with new people doing things slightly differently than their predecessors, they’ve uncovered a few bugs. If any of these can be easily corrected and included with the Vue/Tailwind rollout, please let me know. Otherwise, I just wanted to get a record of these down that we can address in a separate rollout.
>
> 1. The modal on the homepage shows even if no items are tagged to show on homepage (this overlaps with accessibility some since it forms a blank modal)
> 2. Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray.
> 3. Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> 4. The calendars on activity pages are not filtering by age (i.e. youth swimming page shows Master Swim, which is an adult-only class) [I believe you may have already addressed this]
> 5. The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> 6. The location field in the class/event modals is blank (reported previously).
>
> Of those, numbers 2 and 3 are the ones that seem to cause the most issues and might also be easily correctable with a quick change in the Craft CMS settings. If possible to include those in the next release, that would be a huge help. If you feel this will pull you away and cause complications, please feel free to ignore until a better time.
>
> As always, please feel free to track time for these separately. If anything represents sizable work of more than an hour or two, please provide an estimate before proceeding.

==== EMAIL 5 ====
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 14:38:56 -0600
From: Shaun Cooney | Monument Graphics <shaun@monumentgraphics.com>
To:   Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>
Subject: Bugs & Upgrades

Hi Eric,

Over the past few weeks, Aspen has gotten some new people on staff who have started entering data in the CMS. As is typically the case with new people doing things slightly differently than their predecessors, they’ve uncovered a few bugs. If any of these can be easily corrected and included with the Vue/Tailwind rollout, please let me know. Otherwise, I just wanted to get a record of these down that we can address in a separate rollout.

1. The modal on the homepage shows even if no items are tagged to show on homepage (this overlaps with accessibility some since it forms a blank modal)
2. Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray.
3. Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
4. The calendars on activity pages are not filtering by age (i.e. youth swimming page shows Master Swim, which is an adult-only class)
5. The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those?
6. The location field in the class/event modals is blank (reported previously).

Of those, numbers 2 and 3 are the ones that seem to cause the most issues and might also be easily correctable with a quick change in the Craft CMS settings. If possible to include those in the next release, that would be a huge help. If you feel this will pull you away and cause complications, please feel free to ignore until a better time.

As always, please feel free to track time for these separately. If anything represents sizable work of more than an hour or two, please provide an estimate before proceeding.

Thanks,

PLEASE NOTE: I will be out of the office on the afternoon of Tuesday, July 15th, and from Monday, July 21st through Sunday, July 27th.
If you have any deadlines that need met during this time, please let me know as soon as possible so that I can assist you with those before leaving. Thank you!
Shaun Cooney } MONUMENT GRAPHICS | DESIGN + WEB
PO Box 299, Fruita, CO 81521
(970) 242-4311 • MonumentGraphics.com

> > On Sep 9, 2025 at 4:39 AM -0600, Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
> > > I've been researching best ways to prevent the brown outs while minimizing the risk of downtime. Cycling credentials and regenerating composer while effective have a high likelihood of causing problems so I've added this to .htaccess:
> > > # Block common probe targets outright (fast 403)
> > > RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} (?i)^(?:/wp-login\.php|/xmlrpc\.php|/wp-admin|/vendor/phpunit|/composer\.(?:phar|json|lock)|/\.env)$
> > > RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]
> > >
> > > # Block nasty query-string flags used by scanners
> > > RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} (?i)(auto_prepend_file|auto_append_file|allow_url_include|php://input|data://) [OR]
> > > RewriteCond %{THE_REQUEST} (?i)(\=http://|\=https://)
> > > RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]
> > >
> > > # Deny dangerous PHP variants in public
> > > <FilesMatch "\.(phar|phps|phtml)$">
> > > Require all denied
> > > </FilesMatch>
> > >
> > >
> > > These sections should prevent the brown out issues until we get this switched to Servd but we'll need to see it in practice to know for sure. Let me know how the logs look over the next 6-12 hours. We scheduled to have the current version up in Servd by 09/15 so I'm not far off from making that happen which will include launching a clean version of the site.

> On Sep 9, 2025 at 4:39 AM -0600, Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>,
> wrote:
>
> I've been researching best ways to prevent the brown outs while minimizing
> the risk of downtime. Cycling credentials and regenerating composer while
> effective have a high likelihood of causing problems so I've added this to
> .htaccess:
> # Block common probe targets outright (fast 403)
> RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} (?i)^(?:/wp-login\.php|/xmlrpc\.php
> |/wp-admin|/vendor/phpunit|/composer\.(?:phar|json|lock)|/\.env)$
> RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]
>
> # Block nasty query-string flags used by scanners
> RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} (?i
> )(auto_prepend_file|auto_append_file|allow_url_include|php://input|data://)
> [OR]
> RewriteCond %{THE_REQUEST} (?i)(\=http://|\=https://)
> RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]
>
> # Deny dangerous PHP variants in public
> <FilesMatch "\.(phar|phps|phtml)$">
> Require all denied
> </FilesMatch>
>
>
> These sections should prevent the brown out issues until we get this
> switched to Servd but we'll need to see it in practice to know for sure.
> Let me know how the logs look over the next 6-12 hours. We scheduled to
> have the current version up in Servd by 09/15 so I'm not far off from
> making that happen which will include launching a clean version of the site.
>

==== EMAIL 13 ====
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 04:38:53 -0600
From: Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>
To:   Shaun Cooney <shaun@monumentgraphics.com>
Subject: Re: Climb13ers Brown Out

I've been researching best ways to prevent the brown outs while minimizing
the risk of downtime. Cycling credentials and regenerating composer while
effective have a high likelihood of causing problems so I've added this to
.htaccess:
# Block common probe targets outright (fast 403)
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} (?i)^(?:/wp-login\.php|/xmlrpc\.php
|/wp-admin|/vendor/phpunit|/composer\.(?:phar|json|lock)|/\.env)$
RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]

# Block nasty query-string flags used by scanners
RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} (?i
)(auto_prepend_file|auto_append_file|allow_url_include|php://input|data://)
[OR]
RewriteCond %{THE_REQUEST} (?i)(\=http://|\=https://)
RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]

# Deny dangerous PHP variants in public
<FilesMatch "\.(phar|phps|phtml)$">
Require all denied
</FilesMatch>


These sections should prevent the brown out issues until we get this
switched to Servd but we'll need to see it in practice to know for sure.
Let me know how the logs look over the next 6-12 hours. We scheduled to
have the current version up in Servd by 09/15 so I'm not far off from
making that happen which will include launching a clean version of the site.

<li><strong>Residual malicious code or backdoors</strong><span>&nbsp;</span>left over from the hack earlier this year, which may still be consuming resources or exposing vulnerabilities.<br></li>
</ol>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Here are the next cybersecurity steps I recommend we take:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Audit now on Arcustech</strong><span style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">&nbsp;</span><span style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">(looking for suspicious users, files, DB entries).</span></li>
<li><strong style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Rotate Craft admin passwords immediately.</strong></li>
<ul>
<li><span style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">This prevents a hijacked admin from being carried over to Servd.</span><br></li>
</ul>
<li><span style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">We can skip resetting Arcustech DB/SFTP credentials in lieu of migration to Servd, since those will be abandoned once DNS is cut over.</span><br></li>
<li><span style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">On Servd, use freshly generated DB credentials + environment variables.&nbsp;</span><br></li>
<li>Post-migration, review again for hidden users or scripts before going live.<br></li>
</ol>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"></p>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">We can definitely utilize cloudflare to improve&nbsp;security&nbsp;as well. I'll be looking into the best options there, starting with a WAF (firewall for websites).&nbsp;</p>
</div>
<br>

After that,&nbsp;&nbsp;the overall volume of downtime incidents remained higher than normal—even after the patch—but were sporadic. Based on what I see, there are several possibilities but the two most
likely contributing factors to the ongoing downtime are:

   1. *Constant probing and attack traffic* (such as bots scanning for
   WordPress files that don’t exist), which can overwhelm the server.
   2. *Residual malicious code or backdoors* left over from the hack
   earlier this year, which may still be consuming resources or exposing
   vulnerabilities.

Here are the next cybersecurity steps I recommend we take:

   1. *Audit now on Arcustech* (looking for suspicious users, files, DB
   entries).
   2. *Rotate Craft admin passwords immediately.*
      - This prevents a hijacked admin from being carried over to Servd.
      3. We can skip resetting Arcustech DB/SFTP credentials in lieu of
   migration to Servd, since those will be abandoned once DNS is cut over.
   4. On Servd, use freshly generated DB credentials + environment
   variables.
   5. Post-migration, review again for hidden users or scripts before going
   live.

We can definitely utilize cloudflare to improve security as well. I'll be
looking into the best options there, starting with a WAF (firewall for
websites).

Hi Eric,

I spent a little time this evening thumbing through the current logs trying to make heads or tails of what’s going on. Server logs are definitely not my area of expertise, but I think it’s pretty clear from the 404 logs that the site is under fairly constant attempts at being hacked. There’s a lot of reference in those files to Wordpress directories and other generic files not present on the site that bots or malicious humans are attempting to access. This is especially obvious in the 404 error files.

As we go through this process, please keep a keen eye out for signs of hacking. We know for sure the site was hacked back in late May or Early June. Based on the uptime reports, I suspect this happened around June 8th. That’s when an uptick in downtime incidents started. The site was deactivated by Arcustech on June 13th and updated on June 17th. After that,  the overall volume of downtime incidents remained higher than normal—even after the patch—but were sporadic. Then, beginning August 21, multiple downtimes became a daily occurrence. (See attached screenshot showing the downtime reports for this past year). I have not had any success pointing to a change that occurred on Aug 21 that might have caused this—thus another reason I’m concerned it could be a sign of malicious code existing somewhere that’s not been detected.

When I reviewed the site via FTP on June 13th, there were some clearly visible malicious files left in the /public/ directory that I removed, but I’m not 100% confident that’s all that was placed. My fear is that the downtime is tied to leftover or newly placed code from hackers that remain uncaught., but I don’t know quite what to search for, or even where. Do you have much expertise in this area?

In the PHP error log, there’s a distinct change in fatal PHP errors related to the SEO plugin that begin on June 17th. That would seem to point to an issue introduced by the update. Those dates don’t directly correspond to downtime periods though—especially the uptick beginning on August 21, so I’m hesitant to pin the blame there. However, it’s the only lead I have—other than the volume of 404 errors related to what looks like hacking attempts. Do you think the fatal errors in the PHP may be at the root of the brown-outs?

I mainly mention this so that it’s on your mind as we progress with the updates and migration and to see if it sparks any ideas regarding how to tell if there are any lingering bits of malicious code. If you spot any red flags, or have ideas about what/where to check for hacking activity, please let me know. In the meantime, I think it would be prudent to update all IDs and passwords associated with the site. I may need some assistance doing this with the database credentials, so please let me know a good time and we can coordinate that—along with updating the login to the Craft dashboard.

Lastly, the site is also set up to work with a free version of Cloudlfare, so I invited you to that account so that you can see what’s going on there as well.

Thanks as always for your help!

P.S. I sent a check for $2,500 your way as a partial remaining payment for the Vue/Tailwind work with Aspen. Please let me know if that doesn’t arrive in a timely fashion.

The Stretch & Core class at 12:30 on Thanksgiving has been cancelled, but the aria label currently reads: "Press to view event details for Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM”. Instead, for canceled classes, could we change that to: "Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM is canceled. Press to view more details."For closures, the aria label needs to clearly define which facility is closed and when. Ideally, that would read something like “[Facility name] closed from [start time] [date] to [end time][date]. Press [key] for more details”. If that can't reasonably be done, the next best option would be to train Aspen that info needs to be spelled out in the entry title, though it may cause some oddities with the aria labeling still, so we’d need to work that out.It looks like AR-50 and AR-54 on the Google Sheet still need implemented as well: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Fug0Cb-NiWX6tjq33SKhVuWtzuLBsX5V/edit?gid=1316330759#gid=1316330759. Do you recall making any changes to those items?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Moving on to alt text...
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I know Mark put several fallbacks in the code. In some places these are helpful (staff images). In others, they just pull the filename, which would help the site pass an automated scan, but are otherwise useless (e.g. Chess Camp image). The best system I can come up with that would cover what needs coded where would use the following rules, if possible:If the image is representative of a person use the person’s name as the fallback for the alt text. If the image is representative of a place (i.e. facilities, parks, fields, open spaces) use the place name as a fallback for the alt text.In all other cases, the fallback should be a null value (alt=“”). This would define the image as decorative, which is valid in many cases throughout the site and would place the onus on Aspen to make sure the text is entered, rather than rely on iffy fallbacks.We’ll also need to be careful that we’re not forcing entry of alt text for documents or outputting that erroneously for links to PDFs.Do you think that’s achievable?

*1. Adjust aria on date column headings*
If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual dates
in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off as
something like “25. Empty Group.”

*- I did put aria-selected=false on the container and aria-hidden=true on
the child which appears to make the indicator pass over these dates when
tabbing through on Chromium based browsers and Firefox. The arrow keys
don't appear to work when navigating through the indicators.*

*3. Calendar Filters*
Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled open or
closed.
PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on whether the
toggle is open or closed.
NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the filters.

*I ensured these adjustments to the filter--calendar:*

   -

   *Added :aria-expanded to the parent filter button (true/false based on
   dropdown state).*
   -

   *Added :aria-controls on the button and matching id on the panel for
   clear relationships.*
   -

   *Adjusted button aria-labels:*
   -

      *Parents: Toggle {{title}} filter options*
      -

      *Leaf items: Filter by {{category.title}}*
      -

   *Removed redundant* *role*=*"button"* *(native* <button> *already
   exposes the role).*
   -

   *Added* *role*=*"group"* *and an* aria-label *on the dropdown panel to
   give it a name.*
   -

   Hid* decorative icons from AT with* *aria-hidden*=*"true"**.*
   -

   *Escape key closes the open panels.*

*6.* Lindsey also commented on needing to clean up the aria labels for
cancelled activities and closures. Once you get there, please let me know
and I’ll help work through the wording on that. The main goal is to make
sure that the start AND end dates appear for closures and that cancelled
classes are clearly labeled as such.

- This one took a bit of work but I did adjust the "getAriaLabel" to
include cancellations and closure messages. Now that it's working it's easy
to adjust the message if we need.

Pending your review, this should resolve those three items. I'll take a
look at the placeholders / performance issues today for a couple hours then
I'll switch over to Climb13ers for the rest of the day.

The best system I can come up with that would cover what needs coded where would use the following rules, if possible:If the image is representative of a person use the person’s name as the fallback for the alt text. If the image is representative of a place (i.e. facilities, parks, fields, open spaces) use the place name as a fallback for the alt text.In all other cases, the fallback should be a null value (alt=“”). >>>>
>>>>    1. *Adjust aria on date column headings*
>>>>    If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual
>>>>    dates in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off
>>>>    as something like “25. Empty Group.”
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>    IDEAL SOLUTION: Set aria label to read off the full date (i.e.
>>>>    Sunday, November 25th) and have users press (enter or space) to skip to the
>>>>    matching column of activities so users can start tabbing through that day’s
>>>>    activities. This approach would be ideal since it allows users to browse
>>>>    through by day, rather than have them tab through all calendar items.
>>>>    *
>>>>
>>>>    PLAN B: If we can’t make that work, the fallback would be to set
>>>>    the dates in the date row (25, 26, 27, 28…) to aria-hidden=“true.”
>>>>
>>>>    2. *Adjust order of elements within calendar header*
>>>>    Date range (e.g. "November 24 – 30, 2024”) needs to be read first,
>>>>    then next in the order should be the controls to change the date range.
>>>>    Make date range a heading element, if possible.
>>>>    STATUS: COMPLETE - I was able to update the DOM.
>>>>
>>>>    3. *Calendar Filters*
>>>>    Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled
>>>>    open or closed.
>>>>    PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on
>>>>    whether the toggle is open or closed.
>>>>    NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the
>>>>    filters.
>>>>
>>>>    4. *Modal close sends users to beginning of page*
>>>>    Correct behavior would have users return to either the same spot
>>>>    they were at when they opened the modal, or to the next item after that.
>>>>
>>>>    5. *Update aria labels for each event/activity within the calendar*
>>>>    The best way to present that info would be to output the time/day
>>>>    info first, then class, location, and press for more details. I was able to

>>> Hi Eric,

>>> I had a a quick meeting with Lindsey at BeAccessible today. Overall, I
>>> think we’re on the right track with the calendar, but she did have a few
>>> items she said we’d need to adjust. I tackled what I could, but may need
>>> your help with a few things.
>>>
>>>    1. *Adjust aria on date column headings*
>>>    If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual
>>>    dates in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off
>>>    as something like “25. Empty Group.”
>>>
>>>
>>>    IDEAL SOLUTION: Set aria label to read off the full date (i.e.
>>>    Sunday, November 25th) and have users press (enter or space) to skip to the
>>>    matching column of activities so users can start tabbing through that day’s
>>>    activities. This approach would be ideal since it allows users to browse
>>>    through by day, rather than have them tab through all calendar items.
>>>    *
>>>
>>>    PLAN B: If we can’t make that work, the fallback would be to set the
>>>    dates in the date row (25, 26, 27, 28…) to aria-hidden=“true.”
>>>
>>>    2. *Adjust order of elements within calendar header*
>>>    Date range (e.g. "November 24 – 30, 2024”) needs to be read first,
>>>    then next in the order should be the controls to change the date range.
>>>    Make date range a heading element, if possible.
>>>    STATUS: COMPLETE - I was able to update the DOM.
>>>
>>>    3. *Calendar Filters*
>>>    Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled
>>>    open or closed.
>>>    PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on
>>>    whether the toggle is open or closed.
>>>    NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the
>>>    filters.
>>>
>>>    4. *Modal close sends users to beginning of page*
>>>    Correct behavior would have users return to either the same spot
>>>    they were at when they opened the modal, or to the next item after that.
>>>
>>>    5. *Update aria labels for each event/activity within the calendar*
>>>    The best way to present that info would be to output the time/day
>>>    info first, then class, location, and press for more details. I was able to
>>>    adjust the code to do this, but noticed an issue that needs corrected. It
>>>    looks like the method used to obtain ‘plainTextTitle’ on line 555 of the
>>>    CalendarView.vue file doesn’t always work since the activity title isn’t
>>>    always wrapped in a containing element that’s the last child of the parent.
>>>    Do you know of a better way to set the title text? Check the full day camps
>>>    the week of Thanksgiving or Christmas for an example of the errant
>>>    behavior. These events are being pulled from the flex dates section of the
>>>    “Day Camp” event.

>> your help with a few things.
>>
>>    1. *Adjust aria on date column headings*
>>    If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual
>>    dates in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off
>>    as something like “25. Empty Group.”
>>
>>
>>    IDEAL SOLUTION: Set aria label to read off the full date (i.e.
>>    Sunday, November 25th) and have users press (enter or space) to skip to the
>>    matching column of activities so users can start tabbing through that day’s
>>    activities. This approach would be ideal since it allows users to browse
>>    through by day, rather than have them tab through all calendar items.*
>>
>>    PLAN B: If we can’t make that work, the fallback would be to set the
>>    dates in the date row (25, 26, 27, 28…) to aria-hidden=“true.”
>>
>>    2. *Adjust order of elements within calendar header*
>>    Date range (e.g. "November 24 – 30, 2024”) needs to be read first,
>>    then next in the order should be the controls to change the date range.
>>    Make date range a heading element, if possible.
>>    STATUS: COMPLETE - I was able to update the DOM.
>>
>>    3. *Calendar Filters*
>>    Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled open
>>    or closed.
>>    PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on
>>    whether the toggle is open or closed.
>>    NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the
>>    filters.
>>
>>    4. *Modal close sends users to beginning of page*
>>    Correct behavior would have users return to either the same spot they
>>    were at when they opened the modal, or to the next item after that.
>>
>>    5. *Update aria labels for each event/activity within the calendar*
>>    The best way to present that info would be to output the time/day
>>    info first, then class, location, and press for more details. I was able to
>>    adjust the code to do this, but noticed an issue that needs corrected. It
>>    looks like the method used to obtain ‘plainTextTitle’ on line 555 of the
>>    CalendarView.vue file doesn’t always work since the activity title isn’t
>>    always wrapped in a containing element that’s the last child of the parent.

>>    the week of Thanksgiving or Christmas for an example of the errant

>    1. *Adjust aria on date column headings*
>    If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual
>    dates in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off
>    as something like “25. Empty Group.”
>
>
>    IDEAL SOLUTION: Set aria label to read off the full date (i.e. Sunday,
>    November 25th) and have users press (enter or space) to skip to the
>    matching column of activities so users can start tabbing through that day’s
>    activities. This approach would be ideal since it allows users to browse
>    through by day, rather than have them tab through all calendar items.*
>
>    PLAN B: If we can’t make that work, the fallback would be to set the
>    dates in the date row (25, 26, 27, 28…) to aria-hidden=“true.”
>
>    2. *Adjust order of elements within calendar header*
>    Date range (e.g. "November 24 – 30, 2024”) needs to be read first,
>    then next in the order should be the controls to change the date range.
>    Make date range a heading element, if possible.
>    STATUS: COMPLETE - I was able to update the DOM.
>
>    3. *Calendar Filters*
>    Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled open
>    or closed.
>    PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on
>    whether the toggle is open or closed.
>    NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the
>    filters.
>
>    4. *Modal close sends users to beginning of page*

Subject: Re: Wrapping up remaining Aspen Rec Items

Hi Eric,

I had a a quick meeting with Lindsey at BeAccessible today. Overall, I think we’re on the right track with the calendar, but she did have a few items she said we’d need to adjust. I tackled what I could, but may need your help with a few things.

1. Adjust aria on date column headings
If navigating via arrow keys within a screen reader, the individual dates in the date row receive focus and the screen reader reads those off as something like “25. Empty Group.”


IDEAL SOLUTION: Set aria label to read off the full date (i.e. Sunday, November 25th) and have users press (enter or space) to skip to the matching column of activities so users can start tabbing through that day’s activities. This approach would be ideal since it allows users to browse through by day, rather than have them tab through all calendar items.*

PLAN B: If we can’t make that work, the fallback would be to set the dates in the date row (25, 26, 27, 28…) to aria-hidden=“true.”

2. Adjust order of elements within calendar header
Date range (e.g. "November 24 – 30, 2024”) needs to be read first, then next in the order should be the controls to change the date range. Make date range a heading element, if possible.
STATUS: COMPLETE - I was able to update the DOM.

3. Calendar Filters
Screen readers do not alert users when filters have been toggled open or closed.
PROPOSED SOLUTION: use aria-expanded set to true/false based on whether the toggle is open or closed.
NOTE: I made a few adjustments to the aria label attributes for the filters.

4. Modal close sends users to beginning of page
Correct behavior would have users return to either the same spot they were at when they opened the modal, or to the next item after that.

5. Update aria labels for each event/activity within the calendar
The best way to present that info would be to output the time/day info first, then class, location, and press for more details. I was able to adjust the code to do this, but noticed an issue that needs corrected. It looks like the method used to obtain ‘plainTextTitle’ on line 555 of the CalendarView.vue file doesn’t always work since the activity title isn’t always wrapped in a containing element that’s the last child of the parent. Do you know of a better way to set the title text? Check the full day camps the week of Thanksgiving or Christmas for an example of the errant behavior. These events are being pulled from the flex dates section of the “Day Camp” event.

6. Lindsey also commented on needing to clean up the aria labels for cancelled activities and closures. Once you get there, please let me know and I’ll help work through the wording on that. The main goal is to make sure that the start AND end dates appear for closures and that cancelled classes are clearly labeled as such.

*Lindsey recommends implementing a similar action on the activity pages in the activity tables so that users can skip to the next area of the page if they don’t want to tab through the entire table.

If you have any questions, please let me know. I’ll be out most of Wednesday and Thursday, of course, but will try to keep an eye out for any responses if you end up working on it any. Otherwise, I hope you have a great Thanksgiving and we can pick this up next week.

Thanks,

> > > > > > On the aria labels, can we output the date/time to include the day of the week? e.g. “Sunday, November 17 at 9:00AM”. This will help make the audio version of the info match more closely with the visual representation on screen. (NOTE: Keep an eye on the space after the time and before AM/PM. We may need to eliminate that, but I’ll need to find a way to test with JAWS to know for sure).
> > > > > > Please also omit the word “event” (should read: Press to view event details…). I’ll need to confirm it’s correct practice to include the wording “press to view details”. We may need to specify which key needs pressed [enter], or it may be best to leave that off, but I’ll need to talk to BeAccessible to confirm.
> > > > > > Regarding fallbacks for missing locations, we’ll need to look at that as an if/ifelse/else configuration. In Craft, if the location is within the system, it’s a selectable field. Alternatively, there’s an option for the staff to type the location into a text field (see attached). If both of those are not filled, then we should omit the info entirely, rather than saying “At unspecified location.” That could lead to some serious confusion :) Same for time. If not defined, it’s best to just leave it out altogether, rather than say it’s not defined. Title is required, so no need for a fallback there.
> > > > > > From the June 13 email, here’s what I show we still need to fix on the calendar:
> > > > > > Tabbable items on the left side of an open modal have the focus indicator cut off on the left side - I can handle this one, or if you’re in there, I just add a little padding on the left of that column (tailwind pl-2).Location has an empty tabbable item in the open modal - Not sure if this is resolved, but also can’t recall exactly what the issue was. Any ideas?When tabbing through calendar, "enter" doesn't open modal - I think this is fixed. Please confirm.Opening the modal event requires two clicks after the first to open - Still having issues with this. I haven’t figured the pattern out, but the modal sometimes open on 1st click, sometimes it takes two...Please also take a look at the aria labels for cancelled classes and closures. This is a good time of year to test those out. For example, most classes are canceled on Thanksgiving, but visually impaired persons wouldn’t be able to tell using our current method. The Stretch & Core class at 12:30 on Thanksgiving has been cancelled, but the aria label currently reads: "Press to view event details for Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM”. Instead, for canceled classes, could we change that to: "Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM is canceled. Press to view more details."For closures, the aria label needs to clearly define which facility is closed and when. Ideally, that would read something like “[Facility name] closed from [start time] [date] to [end time][date]. Press [key] for more details”. If that can't reasonably be done, the next best option would be to train Aspen that info needs to be spelled out in the entry title, though it may cause some oddities with the aria labeling still, so we’d need to work that out.It looks like AR-50 and AR-54 on the Google Sheet still need implemented as well: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Fug0Cb-NiWX6tjq33SKhVuWtzuLBsX5V/edit?gid=1316330759#gid=1316330759. > > > > > > Moving on to alt text...
> > > > > > I know Mark put several fallbacks in the code. In some places these are helpful (staff images). In others, they just pull the filename, which would help the site pass an automated scan, but are otherwise useless (e.g. Chess Camp image). The best system I can come up with that would cover what needs coded where would use the following rules, if possible:If the image is representative of a person use the person’s name as the fallback for the alt text. If the image is representative of a place (i.e. facilities, parks, fields, open spaces) use the place name as a fallback for the alt text.In all other cases, the fallback should be a null value (alt=“”). This would define the image as decorative, which is valid in many cases throughout the site and would place the onus on Aspen to make sure the text is entered, rather than rely on iffy fallbacks.We’ll also need to be careful that we’re not forcing entry of alt text for documents or outputting that erroneously for links to PDFs.Do you think that’s achievable?

==== EMAIL 43 ====
Date: Wed, 20 Nov 2024 23:26:35 -0700
From: Shaun Cooney <shaun@monumentgraphics.com>
To:   Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>
Subject: Re: Wrapping up remaining Aspen Rec Items

Hi Eric,

My apologies for the delay. I’ve spent several hours diving back into this and trying to make sure I know where all the loose threads are.

Starting with the calendar….

I combed through all the emails and recorded meetings I could find regarding the aria labeling of the calendar, but am missing some of this info. I think most of it was discussed in a Zoom meeting between the two of us on Friday, April 12th. Do you happen to have a recording of that? My follow-up call with BeAccessible was routed through my personal phone, not my business phone, so unfortunately I don’t have a recording of that conversation either. The end result is that I’ll need to run this by BeAccessible again to make sure we haven’t missed anything. I’d like to show them what we have currently, but need to see if we can resolve the following items. Some of these I’m pulling from an email we exchanged on June 13th that contained a list of items we needed to wrap up that I don’t think we ever completed.

1. On the aria labels, can we output the date/time to include the day of the week? e.g. “Sunday, November 17 at 9:00AM”. This will help make the audio version of the info match more closely with the visual representation on screen. (NOTE: Keep an eye on the space after the time and before AM/PM. We may need to eliminate that, but I’ll need to find a way to test with JAWS to know for sure).
2. Please also omit the word “event” (should read: Press to view event details…). I’ll need to confirm it’s correct practice to include the wording “press to view details”. We may need to specify which key needs pressed [enter], or it may be best to leave that off, but I’ll need to talk to BeAccessible to confirm.
3. Regarding fallbacks for missing locations, we’ll need to look at that as an if/ifelse/else configuration. In Craft, if the location is within the system, it’s a selectable field. Alternatively, there’s an option for the staff to type the location into a text field (see attached). If both of those are not filled, then we should omit the info entirely, rather than saying “At unspecified location.” That could lead to some serious confusion :) Same for time. If not defined, it’s best to just leave it out altogether, rather than say it’s not defined. Title is required, so no need for a fallback there.
4. From the June 13 email, here’s what I show we still need to fix on the calendar:
    a. Tabbable items on the left side of an open modal have the focus indicator cut off on the left side - I can handle this one, or if you’re in there, I just add a little padding on the left of that column (tailwind pl-2).
    b. Location has an empty tabbable item in the open modal - Not sure if this is resolved, but also can’t recall exactly what the issue was. Any ideas?
    c. When tabbing through calendar, "enter" doesn't open modal - I think this is fixed. Please confirm.
    d. Opening the modal event requires two clicks after the first to open - Still having issues with this. I haven’t figured the pattern out, but the modal sometimes open on 1st click, sometimes it takes two...
5. Please also take a look at the aria labels for cancelled classes and closures. This is a good time of year to test those out.
    a. For example, most classes are canceled on Thanksgiving, but visually impaired persons wouldn’t be able to tell using our current method. The Stretch & Core class at 12:30 on Thanksgiving has been cancelled, but the aria label currently reads: "Press to view event details for Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM”. Instead, for canceled classes, could we change that to: "Stretch and Core at Red Brick Recreation Center on Nov 28 at 12:30 PM is canceled. Press to view more details."
    b. For closures, the aria label needs to clearly define which facility is closed and when. Ideally, that would read something like “[Facility name] closed from [start time] [date] to [end time][date]. Press [key] for more details”. If that can't reasonably be done, the next best option would be to train Aspen that info needs to be spelled out in the entry title, though it may cause some oddities with the aria labeling still, so we’d need to work that out.
6. It looks like AR-50 and AR-54 on the Google Sheet still need implemented as well: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Fug0Cb-NiWX6tjq33SKhVuWtzuLBsX5V/edit?gid=1316330759#gid=1316330759. Do you recall making any changes to those items?

Moving on to alt text...

I know Mark put several fallbacks in the code. In some places these are helpful (staff images). In others, they just pull the filename, which would help the site pass an automated scan, but are otherwise useless (e.g. Chess Camp image). The best system I can come up with that would cover what needs coded where would use the following rules, if possible:

• If the image is representative of a person use the person’s name as the fallback for the alt text.
• If the image is representative of a place (i.e. facilities, parks, fields, open spaces) use the place name as a fallback for the alt text.
• In all other cases, the fallback should be a null value (alt=“”). This would define the image as decorative, which is valid in many cases throughout the site and would place the onus on Aspen to make sure the text is entered, rather than rely on iffy fallbacks.
• We’ll also need to be careful that we’re not forcing entry of alt text for documents or outputting that erroneously for links to PDFs.

Do you think that’s achievable?

• Slideout arrow should rotate 180º

Activity Pages:

• When Multiple Tabs are active, "Enter" does not switch the tab content. I believe this is fixed, but please confirm.

Modal:

• Tabbing is not trapped - can only be fixed with Vue upgrade, correct?

Dynamically Loaded Content:

• "Soft Refresh" closes navigation - can only be fixed with Vue upgrade, correct?

I'm working on Aspen this week. A recent push to develop resulted in the
project config getting out of sync, which revealed an issue between the
project.yaml and the composer.json. There are four plugins that are
preventing project.yaml from syncing with Project Config in the Settings
section of the Craft dashboard:

   - notifications <https://plugins.craftcms.com/notifications>
   - password-policy
   <https://plugins.craftcms.com/password-policy/changelog?craft4>
   - spoon <https://plugins.craftcms.com/spoon?craft4>
   - webperf <https://plugins.craftcms.com/webperf>

Do you recognize these? Are they still needed? If so, I can add them back
into the composer.json and if not, I'll remove them from project.yaml. The
project.yaml says that spoon and webperf are both set to "enabled: false".

I'd like to get rid of the dead weight but I also want to be very cautious
about what we do and how we do it. Let me know what you think.

<https://plugins.craftcms.com/image-optimize/changelog?craft4=> so updating

command: ```composer require nystudio107/craft-imageoptimize -w && php
craft plugin/install image-optimize``` which brings back the issue we got
stuck on for a month and half back in Jan./Feb., which is accessing the

the command line.

> Any links to assets which are generated dynamically using myAsset->getUrl() in twig or plugins etc will update automatically. So that would cover any assets in Asset selection fields in Craft.
> Any asset URLs in Redactor fields fall into two categories:
>
> 1. If they have an asset ID appended to their URL (Craft adds these as hashes on the end of the URLs) then running an Asset Reindex from within Craft will get those updated to their new URLs automatically.
> 2. If they are not tagged with the asset ID in their URL then they'd need updating manually, or using Craft's find and replace tool which can work well for files or images that aren't using our image transformer service.
>
I’ll need to look into the linking structure we’re currently using a bit to see if that’ll affect Aspen. If you can tell easily please feel free to chime in. Otherwise, I’ll approach both of these as separate projects. Do you have any interest in helping with these?

>>>> In regards to the broken link on activity pages like Hockey, the first
>>>> methodology added vast complexity - adding files, altering yaml, tweaking
>>>> twig files, etc - so I opted to simplify by using a regex to check if it's
>>>> an email or phone entered then adjust to tel or mailto appropriately.
>>>>
>>>> I set a fallback to use what was entered without the link, which I
>>>> thought was a better fallback than nothing or a broken link. Twig and PHP
>>>> are particularly picky about how regex is implemented so I've had to
>>>> wrestle and research a bit the past 12-24 hours but email is now using
>>>> mailto, phone is using tel and the fallback is working if phone and email
>>>> are not triggered now.
>>>>
>>>> Only two files had to change with this method - page--activity and
>>>> phoneNumbers yaml to change the title in the CMS.
>>>>
>>>> This should fix the broken link issue and account for emails being used
>>>> in the future. Craft is updated to show Contact Information as the title of
>>>> the section and "Phone or Email" over the field. I think I have accounted
>>>> for everything but let me know if you see anything else before I bring it

>>> In regards to the broken link on activity pages like Hockey, the first
>>> methodology added vast complexity - adding files, altering yaml, tweaking
>>> twig files, etc - so I opted to simplify by using a regex to check if it's
>>> an email or phone entered then adjust to tel or mailto appropriately.
>>>
>>> I set a fallback to use what was entered without the link, which I
>>> thought was a better fallback than nothing or a broken link. Twig and PHP
>>> are particularly picky about how regex is implemented so I've had to
>>> wrestle and research a bit the past 12-24 hours but email is now using
>>> mailto, phone is using tel and the fallback is working if phone and email
>>> are not triggered now.
>>>
>>> Only two files had to change with this method - page--activity and
>>> phoneNumbers yaml to change the title in the CMS.
>>>
>>> This should fix the broken link issue and account for emails being used
>>> in the future. Craft is updated to show Contact Information as the title of
>>> the section and "Phone or Email" over the field. I think I have accounted
>>> for everything but let me know if you see anything else before I bring it
>>> into the sandbox. Note: there's a test phone number on the hockey page
>>> which I'll remove before pushing to the sandbox.

>> On Jun 28, 2024 at 10:53 AM -0600, Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com
>> <https://mailto:eric@ericphiferllc.com>>, wrote:
>>
>> In regards to the broken link on activity pages like Hockey, the first
>> methodology added vast complexity - adding files, altering yaml, tweaking
>> twig files, etc - so I opted to simplify by using a regex to check if it's
>> an email or phone entered then adjust to tel or mailto appropriately.
>>
>> I set a fallback to use what was entered without the link, which I
>> thought was a better fallback than nothing or a broken link. Twig and PHP
>> are particularly picky about how regex is implemented so I've had to
>> wrestle and research a bit the past 12-24 hours but email is now using
>> mailto, phone is using tel and the fallback is working if phone and email
>> are not triggered now.
>>
>> Only two files had to change with this method - page--activity and
>> phoneNumbers yaml to change the title in the CMS.
>>
>> This should fix the broken link issue and account for emails being used
>> in the future. Craft is updated to show Contact Information as the title of
>> the section and "Phone or Email" over the field. I think I have accounted
>> for everything but let me know if you see anything else before I bring it
>> into the sandbox. Note: there's a test phone number on the hockey page
>> which I'll remove before pushing to the sandbox.
>>
>> Side note: Are we still waiting for approval from Andy to push to
>> production?
>>

>
> In regards to the broken link on activity pages like Hockey, the first
> methodology added vast complexity - adding files, altering yaml, tweaking
> twig files, etc - so I opted to simplify by using a regex to check if it's
> an email or phone entered then adjust to tel or mailto appropriately.
>
> I set a fallback to use what was entered without the link, which I thought
> was a better fallback than nothing or a broken link. Twig and PHP are
> particularly picky about how regex is implemented so I've had to wrestle
> and research a bit the past 12-24 hours but email is now using mailto,
> phone is using tel and the fallback is working if phone and email are not
> triggered now.
>
> Only two files had to change with this method - page--activity and
> phoneNumbers yaml to change the title in the CMS.
>
> This should fix the broken link issue and account for emails being used in
> the future. Craft is updated to show Contact Information as the title of
> the section and "Phone or Email" over the field. I think I have accounted
> for everything but let me know if you see anything else before I bring it
> into the sandbox. Note: there's a test phone number on the hockey page
> which I'll remove before pushing to the sandbox.
>
> Side note: Are we still waiting for approval from Andy to push to
> production?

The gist of the cleanup was to make sure each instance in the admin was using the correct config file, which had limits placed on heading levels and other tools so that the staff would be less likely to break the page's heading hierarchy or introduce inaccessible material. It looks like there’s a relatively “easy” conversion to a new plugin called CKEditor, but I’ve had trouble gleaning if we’ll be able to vary the available heading levels offered in the editor throughout the site. (Redactor used four config files located in 'css › config › redactor’ that were easy to manipulate, then assign to the editors as needed). Since the redactor work needs to be quoted again for 2025, would you have a few minutes to help me ascertain whether we can configure CKEditor in a similar fashion and let me know what you think it would take to convert over to it? I saw mention of global configuration settings, but to make my plan work, I was relying on the ability Redactor had to customize specific instances of the editor using the JSON files. I also saw mention of a couple of issues that we’ll need to keep an eye on:

Redactor is no longer actively maintained which means it no longer gets
security patches - so yes, it is a security vulnerability. If funds are
tight, delaying the migration for up to one year may be acceptable,
provided that regular backups and system tests are conducted. Beyond that,
the risks and costs of delayed migration could outweigh short-term savings.

Moving forward, I felt like we got pushed up against a wall last year with the accessibility work and wouldn’t have been able to meet that deadline without the state’s extension. With that in mind, if you’re able, I’d like to keep moving forward as steadily as possible so that we’re wrapped up well before summer this year. On my end, I’ll have two other Aspen sites (both Squarespace) that I’ll be neck deep in most of Q1 & Q2 in 2025, so I’ll need this site more or less off my plate as soon as possible so that I can adequately focus on those.

The following is a top-level to-do list of items to wrap up accessibility work. In no particular order. Aspen has approved the general scope of work, but I still need to get them a revised estimate.

• **Get caught up on Craft/Plugin updates
• Vue/Tailwind update
• Wrap remaining accessibility items from the original scope of work


The first item is one we haven’t talked about recently but did briefly earlier this year. In past years, Mark had run quarterly updates on the site at a rate of $600/quarter. I recall discussing this with you early last year and you’d indicated this should be do-able on your end, but I wanted to circle back and verify both your availability and the rate. Would this still work for you? Since we’re a bit behind, I anticipate the first update may take a bit more time. If that’s the case, please let me know your expected costs.

When looking into what needs updated, the discontinued redactor plugin caught my eye. That’s the plugin used to create all the rich text editing fields that I was planning on doing some cleanup work on in 2025. The gist of the cleanup was to make sure each instance in the admin was using the correct config file, which had limits placed on heading levels and other tools so that the staff would be less likely to break the page's heading hierarchy or introduce inaccessible material. It looks like there’s a relatively “easy” conversion to a new plugin called CKEditor, but I’ve had trouble gleaning if we’ll be able to vary the available heading levels offered in the editor throughout the site. (Redactor used four config files located in 'css › config › redactor’ that were easy to manipulate, then assign to the editors as needed). Since the redactor work needs to be quoted again for 2025, would you have a few minutes to help me ascertain whether we can configure CKEditor in a similar fashion and let me know what you think it would take to convert over to it? I saw mention of global configuration settings, but to make my plan work, I was relying on the ability Redactor had to customize specific instances of the editor using the JSON files. I also saw mention of a couple of issues that we’ll need to keep an eye on:

1. Possible issues converting target=“blank” links (possibly resolved in current version?).
2. Possible issue converting matrix fields (not sure if this applies?).

Any work needed for this update in particular, please break it out as a separate price from the general updates so that I can include it in the Redactor/Text Editor improvement costs.

Otherwise, are we set for Vue/Tailwind updates with an estimated cost of around $8.5K - 10K?

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> first guess so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> extension is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> updated md filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> encode argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> (the latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> you have a chance to look through it.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> guess so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> extension is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> updated md filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> encode argument.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> (the latest).

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> you have a chance to look through it.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> updated md filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> (the latest).

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> guess so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> (the latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> have a chance to look through it.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> guess so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> have a chance to look through it.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> guess so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> have a chance to look through it.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess
>>>>>>>>>>>>> so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you
>>>>>>>>>>>>> have a chance to look through it.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess
>>>>>>>>>>>> so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have
>>>>>>>>>>>> a chance to look through it.

>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess
>>>>>>>>>>> so it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have
>>>>>>>>>>> a chance to look through it.
>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so
>>>>>>>>>> it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a
>>>>>>>>>> chance to look through it.
>>>>>>>>>>

<div name="messageReplySection">On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer &lt;<a href="mailto:eric@ericphiferllc.com" target="_blank">eric@ericphiferllc.com</a>&gt;, wrote:<br>
<blockquote type="cite" style="border-left-width:thin;border-left-style:solid;margin:5px;padding-left:10px;border-left-color:grey">
<div dir="ltr">Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it took awhile to track down.&nbsp;
<div>The error is:
<div>Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"<br></div>
<div><br></div>
<div>Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode argument.</div>
<div><br></div>
<div>There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).&nbsp;</div>
<div><br></div>
<div>I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a chance to look through it.</div>
</div>
</div>

>>>>>>>>> The error is:

>>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>>> argument.

>>>>>>>>> latest).

>>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a
>>>>>>>>> chance to look through it.

>>>>>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <
>>>>>>>> eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so
>>>>>>>> it took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the
>>>>>>>> latest).
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a
>>>>>>>> chance to look through it.

I can make frontend changes without any issues bringing it into production;

mismatch that occurs. This is because Craft is built so that there's a set
of commands that must be run locally before pushing into the host.

*Bottom line*: I restored production back to before the update this morning
so the project config is synced properly and all the functionality should
be working as before. I need to work in the command line to at least get
those essential commands working then I can push to production properly.

clarifying the process very well and a lot of this fails silently until
production if you don't follow exactly the right steps.

>>>>>>> took awhile to track down.
>>>>>>> The error is:

>>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"

>>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>>> argument.

>>>>>>> latest).

>>>>>>> chance to look through it.

>>>>>>
>>>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it
>>>>>> took awhile to track down.
>>>>>> The error is:
>>>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>>>
>>>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>>>> argument.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).
>>>>>>
>>>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a
>>>>>> chance to look through it.

>>>> On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>,
>>>> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it
>>>> took awhile to track down.
>>>> The error is:
>>>> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter
>>>> "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>>>>
>>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>>> argument.
>>>>
>>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).
>>>>
>>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a
>>>> chance to look through it.
>>>>

Got it. What's happening is that all the emails we're attempting are
getting marked as spam by the "Duplicates" form integration. When I turn
off the duplicates integration the form works as normal.

Duplicates checks for identical form submissions to prevent bots from
spamming submissions; however, the honeypot is active which will trigger
and prevent bot submissions.

This is likely a sandbox issue either because the submissions are coming
from the same IP or because there are trigger words like "test" being used.

I think we're ready to push into production. Worst case scenario I may need
to turn off the duplicate integration.

>>> took awhile to track down.
>>> The error is:

>>> inline_only)"

>>> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is
>>> registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md
>>> filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode
>>> argument.
>>>
>>> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).
>>>
>>> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a chance
>>> to look through it.

> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it took
> awhile to track down.
> The error is:
> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter "md(flavor,
> inline_only)"
>
> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is registering
> an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md filter signature
> in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode argument.
>
> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).
>
> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a chance
> to look through it.

On Jun 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM -0600, Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>, wrote:
> Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it took awhile to track down.
> The error is:
> Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter "md(flavor, inline_only)"
>
> Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is registering an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md filter signature in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode argument.
>
> There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).
>
> I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a chance to look through it.
>

==== EMAIL 137 ====
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 14:46:06 -0600
From: Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>
To:   "Shaun Cooney | Monument Graphics" <shaun@monumentgraphics.com>
Subject: Re: Critical update for Craft

Found it. The problem was not anywhere close to my first guess so it took
awhile to track down.
The error is:
Twig\Error\SyntaxError: Unknown argument "encode" for filter "md(flavor,
inline_only)"

Which is actually coming from Wordsmith. Its Twig extension is registering
an md() filter that conflicts with Craft’s own updated md filter signature
in Craft 4.15+, which no longer supports an encode argument.

There's an explicit fix in 4.4.0 so I updated to 4.5.0. (the latest).

I haven't found anything else yet but let me know once you have a chance to
look through it.

>  • percipioglobal/craft-colour-swatches: If this is used for what I think it is, then it's only used sparingly in the admin to allow users to pick the background color of some of the CTA and callout blocks. The other plugins I don’t recall Mark mentioning and I don’t see mentions of them in our email threads or Basecamp threads so those may take some investigative digging to figure out.  As always, I’ll lean on your recommendations with the mindset of taking the simplest, easiest to maintain approach available.

Please keep me posted with your progress/recommendations on this front and thanks again for your prompt action.

Sounds great, thanks for the update!

I've performed an audit of the versions and dependencies connected with
Craft on Aspen and there are 6 that jump out straight away as problematic.
Three that are abandoned and we'll likely need to remove/replace and three
to keep an eye on:

   - *Redactor*: abandoned. We were already aware of this one, of course,
   and it's on our list to update to CKEditor.
   - *nystudio107/craft-eagerbeaver*: abandoned. Unless it's actively used,
   we should just remove it--I'll have to verify usage.
   - *percipioglobal/craft-colour-swatches*: abandoned. Possible
   replacement with craftpulse/craft-colour-swatches.
   - *verbb/formie*: This one has a major update and possible breaking
   changes.
   - *topshelfcraft/wordsmith*: Major version jump. May involve
   template/function API changes.
   - *craftcms/element-api*: New major version. We should confirm usage
   before updating.

Long story short, there's some breaking changes possible in this version
jump. I've updated in dev this morning and it appears stable. I'll try
sandbox next to ensure things remain stable in the old environment after
updating Craft to the latest in v4 (4.15.6.2 from 4.5.4), but we should
definitely take care of those plugin updates as soon as we've wrapped the
accessibility portion.

I estimate the cost of the Aspen update at $750 if the update runs smoothly.

For your parents' website, there's a few extra steps to restore. Here's
what we'll need to do:

   - *Backups*: database dump and file backups. If it uses Servd and GitHub
   like Aspen then this part should be very easy.
   - *Access the Server*: this will have credentials required to access.
   This process will be different depending on the set up.
   - *Run the composer update*: updates Craft.
   - *Apply Database Migrations*: migrate, sync and clear caches.
   - *Audit for Exploitation*: we'll need to check for unknown admin users,
   malicious code added and check for suspicious plugins/PHP files.
   - *Lock it Down*: as a security precaution, we should reset all admin
   passwords, rotate database credentials and update env secrets.

After this, you'll be solid again. I estimate the cost on this one at $900.
Let me know if this is within your budget, always willing to work with you
on that.

I'm proceeding with the Aspen updates immediately so we can get that
secured.

==== EMAIL 177 ====
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2024 13:16:51 -0600
From: Eric Phifer <eric@ericphiferllc.com>
To:   Shaun Cooney <shaun@monumentgraphics.com>
Subject: Re: Serv’d Updates

Checking into this today for you and it looks like these are the primary
considerations for the upgrade:

   - Where are the DNS Records managed? whois determines this as GoDaddy;
   however, the code indicates Cloudflare may be managing the DNS.
   - servd.dev vanity domain: this is connected with the Development URL
   which was setup at the beginning of this year. No code refers to this. I
   went back and double checked just to be sure.
   - Are private IPs or load balancers being used? I searched the codebase
   and Servd settings for a list of load balancer related terms and none
   indicate the site uses load balancers or private IPs.
   - Primary domain limitation: I verified on Servd > Project Settings >
   Domains that there is only 1 primary domain and 2 subdomains (www &
   sandbox). The only redirect is aspenrecreation.com to
   www.aspenrecreation.com. The docs state that the prompts will indicate
   if an alteration needs to occur.
   - Static files (JS/CSS) are cached by default - we just need to ensure
   static files have a unique name. This can be easily done through the
   webpack config settings.

I tested this extensively with ChatGPT just to double check my work and
determined a step-by-step action plan for the transition. I attached those
PDFs below.

Asset Platform V3:

   - Update all hard-coded asset URLs: there are some throughout YAML files
   that will need to update
   - Custom URL patterns: all url patterns appear to be Servd defaults.
   Docs advise that defaults will not need to be updated.
   - Asset Proxies: searching for any indications of an asset proxy in the
   Servd settings and I see no indication of Cloudflare Worker or any other
   being used.
   - Since no proxy is used, no custom domains need updating.

Additionally, I have successfully logged into CraftCMS admin, updated
composer and webpack in a local environment now. So this is huge progress
into the local dev environment issue.

Basically, the env files were set up for DOS and not Unix, so I had to
convert them.

I also started a new readme file for how to do the setup, still in progress
but hopefully to replace the one on aspen-recreation eventually. I sent you
an invite as a collaborator.

Given the clear steps and progress with the local environment I believe I
can take on the Servd update.

Yes, it does include the deploy, text, Sandbox and publish to production. I
initially thought using the Weglot plugin was the way to go, but I've just
been digging into it and it looks like the plugin is no longer being
maintained. Looks like Weglot instead has a universal integration option
<https://weglot.com/documentation/setup-guides/generic-setup-guide/> that
adds a snippet of JS into the <head> and can also add subdomains to the DNS
config, which helps with SEO - as we said before, likely not necessary. But
this option does have it's own cost, which was not evident in my previous
research - this is their pricing structure:
[image: Screen Shot 2022-10-06 at 8.37.38 PM.png]
There is a monthly option, but the yearly saves 2 months:
[image: Screen Shot 2022-10-06 at 8.39.24 PM.png]
I've gone back to check if there are less expensive or free options, but I
haven't found any that are reliable. There are several like Google Translate
<https://translatepress.com/best-free-website-translation-tool/> that can
translate a full website, but it's a user tool not an integrated plugin and
tends to mess with the design. CraftCMS store has some paid plugin options
<https://plugins.craftcms.com/search?q=translate&tab=plugins&craft4>, but
their reliability is iffy. Weglot still looks like the easiest to work with
and most reliable. Not sure what Aspen Rec's budget is for this but thought
I'd pass on these findings.

Hey Shaun,

Hope your couple of days off were good!

I spoke with Lynne and she conducted an informal poll of her followers. The
response back was extensive, but largely hopeless - they don't think that
Ravelry can be competed with because "Without a full yarn database,
patterns, etc people don't do more than complain about what's missing".
They also brought up two competing sites: fiberocity.com and fiberkind.com.
One is built with Wordpress, the other is built with several technologies
I've never heard of, besides being hosted on DigitalOcean. Compared with
Ravelry, which is built on Rails - clearly they have someone that knows
what they're doing behind the scenes.

Lynne's response was not to bother, but neither of these competing sites
seem to be taking it very seriously. Design can improve, tech behind them
can improve greatly and neither are leveraging the conservative crowd
they're drawing (at least not from the websites). I'm going to reach out to
the two companies just to get an idea of where they are at and what they're
thinking. I don't know if anything will come of it, but it's worth a check
at least - I'll let you know if anything does, but otherwise it looks like
we're tabling this idea.

How are things with Aspen Recreation? I'm continuing to learn and tinker
using their tech.

great documentation. The site is currently on Squarespace, which does
support Weglot. If this is going to be rebuilt on CraftCMS, Weglot does
support Craft via JS integration. CraftCMS does have some native features
for multilingual support - it requires adding a new site for each language
and using a translator for each site.  I can provide an estimate, but I
would need more info before I could provide it with any accuracy - am I
only adding in the widget/plugin, am I building the site based on the
design then integrating multilingual option, are we building with CraftCMS,
Squarespace or something else, etc.
